response.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, CAST(AVG(rental_rate) AS DOUBLE) / AVG(rental_duration) AS per_day FROM film GROUP BY rating), overall AS (SELECT AVG(per_day) AS threshold FROM per_rating), above AS (SELECT p.per_day, p.per_day - o.threshold AS excess FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.per_day > o.threshold) SELECT AVG(per_day) AS avg_per_day_above, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess_above FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: Per-day figure for each rating is AVG(rental_rate) divided by AVG(rental_duration) over that rating's films, as the request literally states. It is not the average of each film's rate/duration ratio. The division is done in DOUBLE so the result is unrounded, since MySQL decimal division would otherwise truncate to a fixed scale.

'Average per-day figure of those ratings' means the mean of the per-day figures of the ratings kept. 'Average amount by which they exceed' means the mean of (per-day figure minus the across-rating average) over the kept ratings. The result is NULL when no rating is kept.

The database is MySQL 8 or later (Sakila-style DDL with TIMESTAMP and BOOLEAN), so CTEs and CROSS JOIN are available. The rating column has no NULL groups in the verified data, so no separate NULL group is produced.
